01_product_sync.summary: The team reviewed last week's numbers: signups rose about 12% and trial-to-paid conversion held at 9%. A proposed Pro plan price cut from $49 to $39 was dropped after support feedback and finance modelling showed losses on accounts under 50 seats. The webinar planned alongside the launch was also dropped to keep the launch simple. Owners and deadlines were set for the mobile login bug fix, survey results, launch checklist, board roadmap and beta user email. The December customer event venue remains unbooked because nobody volunteered.
decisions: Pro plan price stays at $49; the price cut to $39 was scrapped and will be revisited after the integrations ship.
The webinar alongside the launch is dropped; the launch will be kept simple.

actions.task: Fix the login bug on the mobile app
Compile the customer survey results and share them with everyone
Send the launch checklist to Dev so engineering can plan around it
Send the updated roadmap to the board
Write an email to beta users about the new features (sometime next week)
Book the venue for the December customer event

open_questions: Who will book the venue for the December customer event? Nobody has taken ownership.
When to revisit Pro plan pricing, which is after the integrations ship (no date set).

02_client_checkin.summary: Sarah and Ben met with client Priya for a check-in. Because about sixty users now need access and Starter caps at 25 seats, Priya chose the Team plan billed annually and declined the SSO add-on since Google login is sufficient. Sarah will send the formal quote today, and Ben will send the security whitepaper and set up a sandbox workspace by Thursday. Priya will complete the security questionnaire after her finance review, and Ben will book onboarding once the contract is signed.
decisions: Client will go with the Team plan, billed annually (Starter plan dropped).
SSO add-on will not be included; Google login is sufficient for the client.

actions.task: Send the formal quote to Priya
Send the security whitepaper to Priya as soon as I can
Set up a sandbox workspace for Priya's team
Fill in the security questionnaire when she gets a chance, probably after the finance review
Schedule the onboarding session with the client's admins after contract signature
Email Priya a recap of this call right after the call

open_questions: When the client's finance review will be completed and the contract signed is not stated.

03_ops_standup_messy.summary: The Ops stand-up covered the meeting cadence, equipment, reporting, and vendor issues. The team considered moving to bi-weekly meetings but kept the stand-up weekly because a bi-weekly schedule previously caused a supplier issue to be missed. Julie will order replacement monitors, Raj will fix the sales dashboard spreadsheet formulas, Omar will call the vendor about mismatched invoices, and Nina will update the onboarding doc. Nobody took ownership of reporting the broken air conditioning to facilities or of writing last week's minutes.
decisions: Keep the stand-up weekly instead of moving to every two weeks.
Fix the sales dashboard by correcting the spreadsheet formulas rather than rebuilding the report in Python.
